title: Motion in a plane & resolving vectors
examples: How do I find the x and y parts of a force?
If I have two forces at an angle, how do I add them?
What is the difference between vector addition and just adding numbers?

explain.say: Today we learn to break down vectors into parts. These parts are called components. Think of it like finding the separate movements on a map.

draw.text: Motion in a plane & resolving vectors
Vector Components: x and y parts

explain.say: To find the horizontal component, we use the cosine of the angle. The formula is V times cosine of theta. Remember to use the angle correctly.
Next, for the vertical component, we use the sine of the angle. The formula is V times sine of theta. This gives you the y part.
To find the total resultant vector, you add the components separately. You square the x and y parts and take the square root. This gives the magnitude.

faq.q: When do I use cosine versus sine for components?
faq.a: You use cosine for the component next to the angle, which is usually the horizontal part. You use sine for the component opposite the angle, which is usually the vertical part.
asks: Which trig function is for the x-component?
How do I know if I need sin or cos?

faq.q: If the vector is straight up or down, what are the components?
faq.a: If it is straight up or down, the horizontal component is zero. The vertical component is just the total vector length.
asks: What are the components of a vertical vector?
If the angle is ninety degrees, what happens?

faq.q: How do I add two vectors that are not at right angles?
faq.a: You must first break both vectors into their x and y components. Then you add all the x components together and all the y components together.
asks: Do I add the vectors tip to tail?
Is component addition always done separately?

faq.q: What does the resultant displacement mean?
faq.a: It means the single straight line path from the starting point to the ending point. It is the overall change in position.
asks: What is the overall change in position?
Is the resultant the same as the total distance traveled?

faq.q: Do I need to use radians or degrees for the angle?
faq.a: Always check what the question gives you. If it gives degrees, use degrees in your calculator. If it gives radians, use radians.
asks: What is the unit for the angle?

facts: Components break a vector into perpendicular parts, like x and y.
The horizontal component uses the cosine function.
The vertical component uses the sine function.
The magnitude of the resultant vector uses the Pythagorean theorem.
Adding vectors requires adding their corresponding components separately.

quiz.say: A boat travels with a velocity of ten meters per second at an angle of thirty degrees above the horizontal. What is its horizontal component?
quiz.why: The horizontal component is found using the cosine function, which gives the adjacent side in the right triangle formed by the vector.

wrong.0: This is the original magnitude of the vector, not just one component.
wrong.1: This would be half the total velocity, which is incorrect for component resolution.
wrong.2: You used sine instead of cosine, which calculates the wrong component.

quiz.say: A car moves three units east and four units north. What is the magnitude of its resultant displacement?
quiz.why: You correctly used the Pythagorean theorem on the two perpendicular components to find the straight-line distance.

wrong.0: This is the result of squaring both numbers and adding them, forgetting to take the square root.
wrong.2: This is the result of simply adding the two numbers together, ignoring the right angle.
wrong.3: This is the result of subtracting the two numbers, which is not applicable here.

quiz.say: Two forces, one of five newtons at zero degrees and one of five newtons at ninety degrees, are added. What is the magnitude of the resultant force?
quiz.why: You correctly found the x-component (five) and the y-component (five) and used the Pythagorean theorem to find the resultant magnitude.

wrong.0: This suggests the forces cancelled out, which they do not.
wrong.1: This is the result of dividing the total force by two, which is not the correct calculation.
wrong.3: This is the result of simply adding the two forces together, which is only true if they are in the same direction.
